title: Pillars section composition
question: How should Design, supervision, and FF&E read on the homepage? Lock one structure (world stays Parchment Atelier).

options.label: Sticky chapter scroll
options.thesis: The offer title holds while six commitments pass like atelier chapters.
options.viewport: Left: sticky title plus three offer marks Design / Supervision / FF&E. Right: six pillars scroll past as chapter rows with hairline rules.
options.risk: Sticky scroll can feel like a process spine if chapters read numbered.

raised.raise: Three lettered offer views sit above the chapters as the committed cut lines: Design, Supervision, FF&E.
The three offer marks hold as one tensed band so the six chapters read as counterforces, not a feature grid.

options.label: Split atelier ledger
options.thesis: One wide title, then a calm ledger of commitments—no cards, no icons.
options.viewport: Full-width section title on one or two natural lines. Below or beside: six rows title | body with top borders only.
options.risk: Closest to the incumbent; refinement can read as unfinished redesign.

options.label: Contract index
options.thesis: The offer reads like the front page of a contract: indexed proofs, not a feature list.
options.viewport: Wide title. Then a two-column index: meta label + display name, body at full width under each pair.
options.risk: Density can feel legalistic if type scale stays too small.
